How we build a walnut slat wall

Walnut slats change how a room feels more than almost any other single upgrade: warmer, quieter and more finished. We use acoustic slat panels with real walnut veneer on a black felt backing, cut and fitted on site so seams land exactly where the design puts them.

Materials

  • Matching walnut trim and edge profiles
  • Fluted MDF panels painted to match
  • Matte black backing felt
  • Optional integrated LED channels

Options

  • Sound-dampening acoustic backing
  • LED strips between slats or behind panels
  • Floor-to-ceiling or wainscot height
  • Full TV walls or single accent sections

What's included

  • Framing and panel installation
  • TV mounting and concealed cables
  • LED lighting setup where selected
  • Paint, finish and final cleanup

What Tarzana clients ask us

Are the slats real wood?

The visible face is real walnut veneer - actual wood grain, not a print - bonded to an engineered core with an acoustic felt back. It stays straight like an engineered product and looks and feels like walnut because it is walnut.

Do slat walls help with echo?

Noticeably, yes. The felt backing soaks up the reflections that make open rooms sound harsh. Clients notice it most in living rooms with tile or hardwood and in home theaters.

Can slats go around corners and doors?

Corners, outlets and casings are cut and fitted on site. Where a door falls inside the wall, we can face it in matching slats so it disappears into the rhythm.

How are slat walls maintained?

Dust with a microfiber cloth; a slightly damp cloth handles marks. The finish is factory-applied, so there is nothing to oil, wax or reseal.
